correctness.rationale: For every four-normal fan with successive turns strictly in (0,pi), a simultaneous vertex pair must be adjacent and have two-angle turn sum <pi. Opposite pair sums add to 2pi, so all admissible pairs share a pivot. The three other vertices require m incidences each and a direction can supply at most one, proving 3m; a feasible pair plus singleton directions supplies exactly 3m. For parallelograms no pair is feasible and 4m are both necessary and sufficient. Weighted incidence gives fractional values. Every hypothesis, strict boundary and integer multiplicity is covered. Included finite BFS samples are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The primary June 2023 full text covers triangles, parallelograms and regular polygons, but not the non-parallelogram four-vertex case; its lower bound 2m+1 is strictly weaker for m>1. The relevant published-result summaries apply to antipodal or equiangular normal fans and hence to parallelograms in the four-sided case. The angular-star obstruction and resulting integral/fractional rigidity were not in the retrieved statements. Residual priority uncertainty persists.
residual_risks: Published semantic records of the two nearest complementary results were inspected as summaries, not full texts; no claim of whole-document negative coverage is made.
Unindexed research on covering circular-arc incidence systems might contain a broader theorem implying the quadrilateral case.
Search failures are not mathematical proof of universal publication priority.

value.rationale: Completes the exact integral and fractional illumination classification for all genuine convex quadrilaterals, including optimality structure, in the first nonsymmetric four-vertex family not given by the 2023 source; exposes the sharp 3m/4m parallelogram phase boundary and proves no multiplicity discount for any four-sided polygon despite a strict discount already at the regular pentagon for m=2. This is a full natural low-complexity class rather than a choice of arbitrary parameters.
